tips.comment: The most experienced and exposed here, and has the highest rating of 119. Has won over today's trip at Sligo on soft and has run and competed in some decent races, finishing 2nd at Haydock over 15.5f in Grade 2. Last run at Naas, finishing 5th of 8 in Grade 3 over 16f, so today sees a big drop in class. Back up to 18f should also suit.

Good To Be Alive was well beaten last time at Naas but previously won by 6 lengths at Fairyhouse and can easily bounce back. The 4-year-old is stepped up in trip, but if he can handle the better ground, I think he will run a big race in what is a step down in class.
Used to be with Prescott and placed in a decent race for him. Should go well here if recapturing the form and conditions to suit.

Diamond Dealer went close at Doncaster last month when racing keenly, if he settles better he has every chance of taking this. After only eight races he has plenty of improvement to make. The ground suits so I expect a bold show.
Kept on well when winning over a furlong and a half shorter at Haydock last month and should welcome the step up in trip being a point winner over 3 miles.

He won at Hexham in October and is now back on the same mark as that win for the first time since. He won a Class 3 at this track in March last year so he still has ability and could run well, despite a couple of poor efforts recently.
Worth an each-way bet moving up in trip. Disappointing run last time, but the two runs prior to that were decent efforts, including winning at Catterick over shorter.

Wearelongterm had looked like a winner in waiting following two good runs, close 4th in both in May 23, 2m5f good to soft here and 2m6f Cartmel good. Was then off for 540 days and on 3rd start back (3 starts ago) showed he retained ability when 2nd over 3m Wetherby, even if the trip stretched him. If forgiven for last two starts (heavy ground and a chase), the return to hurdles back here could see a return to better form.
Won a few runs ago. Needs to run to that level here, as has been unplaced a few times recently. CD to suit.

I think the rate the trainer has placed this horse with a great opportunity to continue winning. They put a young apprentice on board who can claim a 7 lb off the weight, which must give a great chance.
Winner over a shorter trip at this track back in November. Has run well over trips similar to this of late, including last time out when just weakening out of it at a stiffer track in Carlisle.

Top weight in here, but has form to be competitive despite the welter weight. Obviously, yard form is a bit of a worry, but I feel they've turned a corner the last few days, with some going close and a few getting their heads in front in the last few days. She's only managed to get her head in front once over fences, beating now stable mate So Des Flos comfortably, with a 4L gap separating them at the line. She pulled clear to win cosily. She ran a great race on stable debut reverting back to hurdles, beating Blaze The Way easily, with recent Plate 2nd Thecompanysergeant back in 3rd place. That's decent enough form. She pulled up in the Kim Muir last time out. She never went a yard, to be fair. Ignoring that run, with her sights massively lowered here, this looks a good opportunity to get her head in front if the weight doesn't harm her chances.
Has been out of form this season, but ran up a 4-timer last year, culminating in winning the Eider Chase from a mark just a pound lower than what he runs off today. Worth an each-way bet.
Saint Arvans is a previous winner of this race. Today's ground conditions will be just fine and a big run will be anticipated.
Been off a while, but ran third a few runs back and then won on his next outing. Conditions will suit, and the horse can still improve.

She may have only won 1 of her 7 starts over hurdles, she has been fairly consistent, with a recent record of 2nd, 3rd, 4th with the 2nd coming at this track. She is on the same mark as that day and could run well dropped in class having stepped up to Class 2 company last time out.
Good second a few runs back and has been unplaced since then. Still early days for this horse, and Ellison does well at this track. Could go well.
Deerstalker looks competitive in this Hunter Chase at Kelso today. He should be on the premises throughout and is expected to go in.
Good second last time out. This trip should suit, and the conditions will be in his favor. This draw isn't too bad.
Not the strongest looking of races and The Hatchet looks to be the best of the bunch. 4/10 at Ayr in March on soft. The drier ground should suit him and his breeding.
Well-bred horse who lacks experience. Looks well-bred and could have too much class for this lot if on a going day.

This Time Test filly boasts a pedigree that includes a half-sister to the notable winner The Organiser, who has shown his prowess up to 7f, and the 2-year-old 1m winner Rosardo Senorita. Her dam, though unraced, is a half-sister to the capable 2-year-old winner Tiger Eye, who excelled at 7f. With the capable S. Kirrane riding and odds set at 33/1, an each-way bet on this filly could be a wise choice.

Ottoman has a first start for a yard more known for runners over the jumps but is very interesting on the best of its form in Ireland. He has run well in nurseries there and is on a great mark if the move has worked.
Amber Honey is another that has had three ordinary C5 starts so far. As a result, she is coming into this handicap debut on a decent opening mark and worth a shot now dropping to C6.
Pallas Lord has had a lot of runs recently, so may be a bit exposed. He finished runner-up favorite in his last two, and a chance is taken at good odds for him to go one better here.

Havana Prince won 3 times last season, including over course and distance last July. That was his last start of 2024, and though he has been well beaten in his two starts this year, he looks a good each way bet returned to 7 furlongs at Redcar.

Highland Olly ran better than the result suggested on his final start of 2024, not getting a clear run when beaten just over 5 lengths at Southwell. Prior to that he was in good form, including a narrow win off 64 at Musselburgh, and he’s been eased 1lb since. He’s gone well fresh before and if tuned up, he’s very much in the mix back on turf.
Coming back from a 111-day break. Now 5lb below last winning mark. Distance winner, so no issues with the trip and has form in different grounds. Each way.
Placed a few runs ago and has held his form well. Generally, still a very unexposed horse with a lot to learn, but could have too much class for them.

Alfie Boy last won here a year ago when running off a 64 in C6 at 7f. Although not great for the last three runs, they were at 1 mile and 1m7f. I think the return here back at 7f with Amie in the saddle off a 58 could be worth an EW 4P.
Great Blasket has not won since last June but has dropped to that last C3 winning mark and has the very handy Alex Voikhansky in the saddle, claiming 3 lbs.

Empire Of Light was solid last season and signed off with a respectable fourth at Doncaster, staying on over 7f. He’s been crying out for a return to 1m, which he stays well, and should be sharp enough to go close if tuned up after the break. Reliable type who rarely runs a bad race.
Good morning! Alex returns after a six-month break. He won five races from eleven last year and has gone well fresh in the past. Could surprise at decent odds.

A Michael Dods trained 5-year-old who has had 19 races on the flat, winning 3 times and has finished in the frame 7 times. His last win was in July last year on a class 5 handicap over 1 mile at Ayr on good going when staying on at the finish to win by 1 1/4 lengths. He is in a class 3 handicap over 1 mile on good going and had Connor Beasley in the saddle, who has ridden him before. This gelding has been off track for 185 days but has run well when fresh before. He is a winner over this distance on similar going and is a good e/w shout at a good price in this race today.
Won two of his last six. Still potentially well handicapped on old form and sure to run well if on a going day. The conditions might help.
Good 3rd last month in a bumper. Dropped in trip, got flat debut, and looks to have a good each-way chance in an open-looking race. Stable in form.
Lightly raced and well-bred, looks sure to go well with conditions in his favor. The trainer does well at the track and could go well.
In a weak-looking race, it may pay to side with this one who could be well-handicapped and will probably love these conditions.

Didaar showed promise on handicap debut back in September in C4 off an 84. While the last two runs have been pants, they were on soft ground. I think the return to firmer ground today off a 75 could be worth a chance.

Watermelon Sugar is flying right now, winning impressively at Lingfield then backing it up with a strong second off a higher mark. He’s clearly thriving and although the drop to 5f is a slight unknown, he’s in such good form that he should be right in the thick of it again if things fall right.
Good 4th two starts back. Wouldn't need to improve much to get involved and CD to suit. Good chance at the weights too.

Slowdownbarney came from the rear to go down narrowly over 2m at Dundalk last time, matching the pick of his Irish form. First run on Tapeta but the trip suits well, and with a strong jockey booking, he looks a proper contender if taking to the surface.
Not done much so far, but at least has experience. Has run better than the results suggest and is well drawn here to go well.

Trad Jazz made a lovely start when winning on debut over 8f here, doing it comfortably despite showing signs of inexperience. The step up in trip looks like a good move and with the yard in form, he’s tough to look past with plenty more likely to come.

Dixieland Blues made a solid impression when second on debut at Southwell and looks the type to improve plenty for that. Trainer’s going well and although she’s coming back from a break, she’s an obvious player if ready to roll.
Definitely better bred than most of these. The trainer does well on the AW and could go well here with CD to suit.
Good 4th last time out. This race isn't much tougher. The connections of this one are in decent form, and the draw will help this one run well.

Won a similar race over 7f around here back in August from a 2lb lower mark, so is right there on the numbers. Was given too much to do and had a troubled passage last time. The expected strong pace will help him here stepped back up to a mile, as will Loughnane being back on top as he was when the selection won at Kempton last August.

Crack Shot changed hands for 80,000 gns and has been kept fresh for his first start for trainer D Kubler having been off for 176 days, I would be surprised if they don't recoup any of that money here tonight and he's already been well backed.

I would expect a better showing from Pjanoo today as last time he was too far off the pace and tired without even getting close. It's his first run for his new trainer and Rossa Ryan is booked for the ride and he will likely lead from the start and might be hard to peg back.

Hieronymus got the job done last time over 7f here and loves to bowl along in front. He’s up in trip but has a solid record at the track and still looks fairly treated on his best form. Should be right in the mix again if allowed to dictate.
Unplaced in his last three starts, but before that was third in a decent race. He is sure to go well if rediscovering that form.

KING CABO has run well fresh before and now drops in grade on his return to the all-weather. Probably didn't enjoy the soft stuff on the flat at the end of last season, so might be able to progress further this season in favourable conditions and at preferred tracks. Kempton is one of those and he could outrun this price against lesser opposition.

Future Cutlet shaped well enough at Dundalk last time despite having too much to do and now joins a new yard that might get more out of him. He’s down in trip and while his best form is on turf, there’s enough there to suggest he could run a big race first time up if things click.

Tattie Bogle looked like she had more in the tank when winning at Newcastle last time, doing it nicely without being fully extended. First time on Polytrack and back from a break, but now in handicaps and open to improvement, she looks a real threat if handling the surface.

This James Owen-trained 5-year-old gelding won on his penultimate start over one mile six furlongs at Southwell and was only beaten 1 1/4 lengths in fourth place behind the B Brookhouse-trained Cardano in his latest start over one mile six furlongs at Wolverhampton. Despite finding trouble in running and with Hector Crouch back onboard, he should go well tonight.

Artisan Dancer hasn’t been at his best lately and was never in it from a wide trip at Wolverhampton, but he’s back from a break and finally starting to look better treated by the handicapper. Up in trip and could be a contender if the freshen-up has done the trick.

Comfortable winner of this race last year, so Cinnodin is played in the hope of a repeat performance. Runs off a mark 4 lbs below last year's winning rating of 76. Decent second over course and distance on return here last year in September. Last two races have the look of the horse getting back to full fitness. Won this race with a burst of late speed last year. Can get involved.
